item.title: The AuDHD Strength of Being Unified
item.description:
Autism

The AuDHD Strength of Being Unified

Experiencing the world through connection and meaning.

Posted May 9, 2026

Key points
  • Unified AuDHD thinking connects ideas, emotions, and systems into meaningful patterns.
  • Unified thinkers often bring clarity through holistic, cross-disciplinary understanding.
  • When supported, unified AuDHD strengths foster identity, insight, and leadership.

This article is the second in a five-part series exploring strengths associated with coexisting autism and ADHD. Without minimising the real challenges of AuDHD, the series draws on clinical practice and research to highlight strengths from a person-centred, strengths-based perspective. Read Part 1 here.

In my post Understanding Strengths With Coexisting Autism and ADHD (Storace, 2025), I describe five interconnected capacities through which difference becomes depth: attuned, unified, dynamic, heartfelt, and driven. One of the most conceptually rich of these is the quality of being unified—a capacity to integrate, connect, and synthesise experiences into coherent understanding.

Understanding “Unified” as a Strength

To be unified is to experience life through connection rather than compartmentalisation. While some minds work by separation and categorisation, the unified mind operates through synthesis, linking ideas, experiences, emotions, and systems into a larger, articulated whole.

For many individuals with AuDHD, this is not a conscious strategy; it is an intrinsic way of processing the world. It often manifests as an ability to:

  • See hidden patterns
  • Recognise how seemingly unrelated issues connect
  • Understand problems systemically rather than in isolation

Unfortunately, in educational and professional contexts that prioritise speed over synthesis, or compartmentalisation over coherence, this strength can be misunderstood as “overthinking,” “going off topic,” or even “lack of focus.” Yet what appears as divergence is often a deep integrative process underway.

In clinical contexts, I often observe that when individuals with AuDHD are encouraged to articulate their unified thinking rather than suppress it, what initially seems complex becomes clear, not only for themselves but also for those around them.

Four Dimensions of the Unified Experience

Source: Keith Storace

1. Integrative Thinking and Synthesis

The unified mind weaves information together. People with this strength tend to absorb ideas from multiple sources and connect them into a cohesive, meaningful whole (Taylor et al., 2023).

This can manifest as an ability to:

  • Bridge different viewpoints
  • Find coherence in complexity
  • Create narratives that help others make sense of confusing situations
article continues after advertisement

While this can sometimes seem slower than linear thinking, it is often deeper. Unified thinkers are not racing towards answers; they are constructing frameworks of meaning (Antshel & Russo, 2019).

When this ability is nurtured, it becomes a form of intellectual and emotional leadership, helping communities move from fragmentation to understanding.

2. Holistic Understanding of Relationships

Unified individuals rarely experience relationships in isolation. They perceive social systems rather than individual roles. This enables them to:

  • Sense group dynamics
  • Understand family or team patterns
  • Recognise how emotional responses can shape the wider social environment

In relationships, this can lead to deep compassion and insight. However, it can also become burdensome if the individual feels responsible for holding everyone else’s emotional landscape together.

From a therapeutic standpoint, supporting unified individuals often involves helping them maintain connection without feeling responsible for holding everything together.

article continues after advertisement

3. Cross-Disciplinary Creativity

Unified thinkers often move naturally across fields—philosophy and psychology, science and art, ethics and technology. This cross-disciplinary flow does not stem from indecision but from the ability to see how different knowledge systems inform one another.

This strength is particularly valuable in a world that increasingly demands transdisciplinary problem-solving: climate change, mental health systems, education reform, and social justice cannot be addressed from siloed perspectives alone.

Individuals with a unified AuDHD style often feel most alive in spaces where integration is valued over specialisation.

4. A Cohesive Sense of Identity

On a personal level, unification is not merely cognitive—it is existential. Many individuals with AuDHD struggle with identity fragmentation after years of masking, misdiagnosis, or attempts to “fit in.”

The unified strength supports

  • Integration of multiple life experiences
  • Reconciliation of different self-aspects
  • Development of a coherent and authentic identity

This is why, therapeutically, helping an individual recognise their unified capacity often leads to significant shifts in self-understanding. Rather than feeling scattered, they begin to see themselves as coherent, complex, and whole.

Unified Strength in Education

In educational contexts, students with a unified cognitive style often differ from standard learning expectations. Traditional education tends to reward linear progression and compartmentalised learning, whereas unified learners naturally connect ideas across subjects, years, and experiences.

Students with this strength often:

  • Make conceptual leaps between unrelated topics
  • Struggle with rote or fragmented tasks
  • Excel in conceptual and theoretical subjects (philosophy, psychology, systems science, social sciences, design, environmental studies)
  • Ask questions that challenge strictly linear curricula
article continues after advertisement

They may sometimes be labelled as “going off-topic” when, in fact, they are mapping a broader system of meaning.

Practical Implications for Education

Educators can support unified learners by:

  • Encouraging interdisciplinary learning opportunities
  • Allowing students to demonstrate understanding through integrative projects rather than isolated tests
  • Validating systems-thinking rather than forcing purely linear responses
  • Supporting conceptual mapping, mind-mapping, and cross-subject exploration

When unified learners feel their integrative thinking is valued, their engagement often deepens, and their academic confidence strengthens significantly.

Unified Strength in Employment

In workplaces, unified thinkers are often the bridge-builders, systems integrators, and big-picture thinkers (Crook & McDowall, 2024). They are frequently the ones who spot problems before they escalate and notice connections others miss.

People with a unified AuDHD profile often thrive in:

  • Strategic planning roles
  • Systems analysis
  • Therapeutic and counselling professions
  • Education, design, architecture, policy, and leadership
  • Research and complex problem-solving environments

They bring the capacity to see how individual roles function within a larger system and often act as informal integrators within teams.

Practical Implications for Employers and Organisations

To harness unified strengths, organisations can:

  • Involve individuals in big-picture planning
  • Encourage cross-team collaboration
  • Recognise pattern recognition and systems insight as leadership assets
  • Allow space for reflective thinking alongside action
article continues after advertisement

Unified thinkers often prove invaluable when workplaces recognise that integration is foresight.

Holding Complexity Together

Unification offers a way of making sense of the world through connection, pattern, and coherence. When educational and workplace cultures allow space for integrative thinking, reflective depth, and conceptual mapping, this way of processing can be lived with greater ease and self-trust. In this, the unified experience within AuDHD is recognised as part of the natural diversity of human cognition, with understanding, identity, and meaning held in continuity and respect.

item.title: Pros and Cons of the 'Grim Keeping' Dating Trend
item.description:
Mating

Pros and Cons of the 'Grim Keeping' Dating Trend

Sharing your dislikes can have its positives and negatives.

Posted May 9, 2026

Key points
  • Grim keeping in dating is when you connect romantically with someone over shared dislikes rather than likes.
  • It can help you connect with each other by allowing for mutual validation and support, and more authenticity.
  • Grim keeping can lead to dwelling too much in the negative and the wrong relationship dynamics.
  • Be mindful of how much time you spend in the negative as opposed to the positive, and do what feels right.
Grim keeping is when you connect romantically with someone over shared dislikes rather than likes.
Source: silverkblack/Getty

You may have heard it said that there is a thin line between love and hate. Well, what's been dubbed "grim keeping" is about forming a direct line between hate and love when dating.

That's because grim keeping is when you connect romantically with someone over shared dislikes rather than likes. I already mentioned this term briefly in "A Funny Bone to Pick" back when I did a rundown of five different dating trends for 2025. Grim keeping may be keeping with the times since these days it seems like a lot of people are bonding over complaining about the current state of society.

There are certainly things to like about sharing dislikes. You can garner some real positives from the negatives. But the grim reality is that you've got to be wary about the potential negatives of being, well, too negative.

The Advantages of Grim Keeping

First the positives. Grim keeping can be very effective at building connection because it plays into some typical human tendencies. One of these tendencies is to prioritize identifying and dealing with threats above all else, natural programming that has helped humans survive threats like lions, floods, sweater vests, and fruitcakes throughout the ages. That's why someone complaining about the same threat that you may face is likely to get your ears to naturally perk up and listen.

A second tendency is gravitating toward the "us versus them" mentality. As social animals, we prefer facing threats with allies rather than alone. When there is seemingly a common enemy, it is easier to move beyond differences and instead team up to create a united front.

A third tendency is taking the easy way out rather than working at something. Yep, surprise, surprise, humans can be quite lazy. It can be a whole lot easier to complain about problems than find solutions, to criticize rather than do. You can always find some kind of fault in anything or anyone. If every complaint were actually followed by a solution, we'd have a whole lot fewer problems around us.

Grim keeping can also provide rather immediate benefits to both of you. One is validation and support—the comfort that you are not alone in disliking someone or something and that your negative feelings are justified. It is not your fault, for example, that your boss berates you, that you feel down, or that you used that fruitcake that your friend gave you as a doorstop. You can listen to each other's complaints and share solutions, like ways to use that fruitcake that don't involve putting the fruitcake into your mouth.

article continues after advertisement

Grim keeping can be about being more authentic as well. When you reveal what you don't like, you can be shedding your manicured, oh-everything-is-great facade. When the other person does that too, it can open both of you up for deeper connections.

Moreover, it does help to find out what the other person dislikes. This is part of getting to know who the other person really is, beyond the fact that he or she likes long walks on the beach. If part of the person's dislikes includes who you really are, then that's certainly useful information. Regardless, more knowledge about the other person's dislikes can help you better deal with them in the future if your interactions continue to go positively and lead to a relationship.

The Disadvantages of Grim Keeping

Now that we've covered the potential positives of grim keeping, let's complain about it, shall we? A risk is being too, um, negative, which can be a real downer. That may not be a great way of starting off a relationship. Whenever you see the other person, might your first instinct be going forward, "Gee, what can I complain about next?"

And that next thing for the other person could very well be you. If someone is complaining a whole lot about other people, what makes you think that you will always be immune or the exception? One day, that person could end up grim keeping with someone else about you.

You also don't want to end up being no more than the other person's support hotline or therapist. Being someone's hotline is not the same thing as being thought of as hot. Plus, it can create a dependent relationship rather than one with two independent people who choose to be with each other.

Another risk is that grim keeping can keep you from actually solving problems. It can keep both of you in the complaining phase. Or the blame game, where you keep blaming others for your problems instead of fixing what needs to be fixed about yourself.

In general, dwelling too much on the negative can attract people who are overly negative and pessimistic. At the extreme, such people can have real hatred against certain groups of people and espouse isms like racism or agism. Yep, racists aren't exactly the happiest of people. It can also attract those with issues that need real professional help to address. And presumably, racists or potential patients are not what you are looking for in dating.

article continues after advertisement

How to Handle Grim Keeping

Therefore, it is a good idea to keep rough track of how negative versus positive you are during your interactions with the other person. One of the keys to life is balance, not going too far in either direction. There is a difference between being authentic and being authentically negative,

Also, put a limit on how often you bring up the same complaints over and over again without taking positive steps toward a solution. Sure, such-and-such job, boss, coworker, politician, or whatever sucks. But it's not as if it's going to magically change until you actually take some positive steps.

Finally, as is the case with all dating trends, adopt grim keeping only if and when it comes naturally to you. Don't be grim simply on a whim that it might resonate with the other person. Dating is about finding the right mutual fit and not about one person winning the other over. Don't waste your time with someone who is wrong for you, which will mean less time for someone who is right for you. So, if a date ends up negatively—meaning it doesn't work out—then that may be a positive thing for you in the long run.
